correctness.rationale: The exact defining free-p molecular decomposition equals a finite weighted flow optimization. Concavity along cycle circulations removes every cycle without increasing p-cost; therefore all four-point norms minimize over precisely 16 spanning trees. Exact bilinear midpoint secants reduce the global Lipschitz constant to normalized tangents. Reflections reduce direction signs to nonnegative. Two explicit cycle eliminations each give three nonnegative unit-edge coefficients summing one, and one representation has largest coefficient at least 1/2; concave Karamata bounds p-cost by 2(1/4)^p+(1/2)^p. The interior midpoint derivative at (1/4,1/4) in direction (1/2,1/2) has masses (-3/4,1/4,1/4,1/4). All 16 cut-flow trees are exhaustively enumerated with rational costs; every sorted profile dominates (1/4,1/4,1/2) and the latter occurs. The target value follows for every real p in (0,1], including the p=1 endpoint. verify_square.py replays all finite computations; its sampled parameter checks are not treated as continuum proof.

value.rationale: The four-vertex square is the first genuinely multidimensional cell of the coordinatewise-affine construction used to obtain Schauder bases for free p-spaces. Existing papers provide nonmatching bounds for the canonical retraction. The result closes the natural local sharp-constant problem for every quasi-Banach exponent and explains a mixed-direction extremizer via three edge transport loads (1/2,1/4,1/4), which is invisible to one-coordinate bounds. Exactness supplies a concrete benchmark for studying higher-dimensional and multi-cell constants, without asserting such further theorems. This is more than a textbook deduction or arbitrary finite tabulation because the global analytic upper bound is structural and the benchmark was unprovided by close predecessors.
